chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Sabbah al-Hadda’ who said:

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: When you intend to travel, stand at the door of your house and recite the Opening of the Book (Surah al-Fatiha) in front of you, and on your right, and on your left, and say 'He is Allah, One' (Surah al-Ikhlas) in front of you, and on your right and on your left, and say 'I seek Refuge in the Lord of the people' (Surah al-Nas) and say 'I seek Refuge in the Lord of Al-Falaq' (Surah al-Falaq) in front of you, and on your right and on your left, then say: 'O Allah, protect me and protect what is with me, and keep me safe and keep safe whatever is with me, and deliver me and deliver what is with me with an excellent delivery'.

Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Have you not seen the man who is protected but what is with him is not protected, and he is safe but what is with him is not safe, and he reaches (his destination) but what is with him does not reach?'.

key_terms.أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ: I seek Refuge in the Lord of the people (Surah Al-Nas)
key_terms.أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الْفَلَقِ: I seek Refuge in the Lord of Al-Falaq (Surah Al-Falaq)
key_terms.فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ: The Opening of the Book (Surah Al-Fatiha)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication and ritual for traveling in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi emphasizes the spiritual preparation for travel by invoking divine protection through the recitation of the 'Four Quls' and Al-Fatiha in all directions, symbolizing comprehensive coverage of safety. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the interconnection between the traveler's personal well-being and the security of their possessions, urging a holistic supplication for both. The practice reflects the tradition of seeking Allah's guardianship before embarking on journeys, a common theme in Islamic piety.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Musa Bin Al Qasim, from Sabbah Al Haza’a who said,

‘Abu Abul Hassanasws said: ‘Whenever you intend the journey, so pause at the door of your house and recite the Opening of the Book (Chapter 1) in front of you, and on your right, and on your left, and [112:1] Say He Allah is One (Chapter 112) in front of you, and on your right and on your left, and [114:1] Say I seek Refuge in the Lord of the people (Chapter 114) and [113:1] Say I seek Refuge in the Lord of Al Falaq in front of you, and on your right and on your left, then say, ‘O Allahazwj! Protect me and Protect what is with me, and Keep me safe and Kee safe whatever is with me, and Deliver me and Deliver what is with me (to my destination) with an excellent Delivery’.

Then he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘But, have you not seen the man who is protected and what is with his is not protected, and he is safe and what is with him is not safe, and he reaches (his destination) and what is with him does not reach?’.
en.sarwar: 9. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Musa ibn al-Qasim from Sabbah al-Hadhdha’ who has said the following:

“Abu al-Hassan (a.s.) has said, ‘When you like to travel, stand at the door of your house and recite Chapter one of the Holy Quran to your front, right and left and Chapter 1 12 of the Holy Quran to your front, right and left. Chapter 114 of the Holy Quran and Chapter 113 to your front, right and left, then say, “O Lord, protect me and protect that which is with me, grant me safety and that which is with me, help me reach my destination and that which is with me in a good arrival.’”

“The Imam then asked, ‘Have you ever thought that a man is protected but not that which is with him, a man is safe but not that which is with him and a man arrives his destination but not that which is with him?”’
